options.metric: police-reported crashes per nominal clock-hour (crash count divided by calendar days in the included years times the hours in the time category)
options.denominator: nominal clock-hours represented by 2013–2025: 66,472 Day hours (14 per calendar day) and 47,480 Night hours (10 per calendar day); no exposure-to-traffic denominator
options.grouping: Night (20:00–05:59), Day (06:00–19:59), and Unknown time (missing or unclassifiable crash_time)
options.reason: A per-clock-hour comparison corrects for Night and Day covering different numbers of hours while showing reported crash frequency.
options.answer: Across complete years 2013–2025, NYC had 11.05 reported crashes per nominal nighttime clock-hour versus 24.18 per daytime clock-hour.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether reported-crash frequency is higher at night after accounting for unequal clock-time windows: across complete calendar years 2013–2025, Night (20:00–05:59) averaged 11.05 police-reported crashes per nominal clock-hour (10 hours/day) versus 24.18 for Day (06:00–19:59; 14 hours/day), with Unknown time a zero-count group. It is defensible as a comparison of crash volume per nominal clock-hour, using included calendar days multiplied by each band's hours (47,480 Night hours and 66,472 Day hours). It cannot establish per-trip, per-mile, or exposure-adjusted street danger, and nominal hours ignore daylight-saving clock changes. The check found 136,969 rows (6.0% of valid-date records) from partial 2012 and 2026 excluded, no missing or unclassifiable times, and 23,787 midnight records (1.1% of included rows) retained in Night because midnight may be default-coded.

options.metric: sum of number_of_persons_injured and sum of number_of_persons_killed separately, each per 1,000 complete-case crashes
options.denominator: complete-case crash count in each time category (rows nonmissing on both person outcome columns)
options.grouping: Night (20:00–05:59), Day (06:00–19:59), and Unknown time (missing or unclassifiable crash_time)
options.reason: Injury and death burden per crash directly compares the reported consequences of crashes at night and during the day.
options.answer: Among reported crashes, nighttime crashes involved 404.01 injured and 3.08 killed people per 1,000 crashes, compared with 308.72 injured and 1.12 killed during the day.
options.interpretation: This framing addresses whether reported crashes have more serious consequences at night: among complete-case crashes in complete calendar years 2013–2025, Night (20:00–05:59) had 404.01 persons injured and 3.08 persons killed per 1,000 crashes, versus 308.72 injured and 1.12 killed for Day (06:00–19:59); Unknown time had no records. Outcomes are the separate sums of number_of_persons_injured and number_of_persons_killed divided by crashes with both values present in that time category, multiplied by 1,000, making this a defensible comparison of burden conditional on a reported crash. It cannot determine danger per trip or mile because traffic and exposure volumes are absent. The check found 136,969 valid-date rows (6.0%) in partial 2012/2026 excluded; among 2,132,218 complete-year candidates, 18 lacked injury values and 36 lacked death values (42 lacking either, 0.002%) and were excluded, while the final population had 23,786 midnight records (1.1%) kept in Night despite possible default coding; no times were missing or unclassifiable.
